category_title: Struggling students using infinite practice for mastery
minimal_context: The student is working in a computer lab session with the goal of getting five-in-a-row on their assigned math skills.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are 20 minutes into the computer lab session. Please keep working on your assigned skills to reach the goal of getting five-in-a-row.

STUDENT: I'm working on it. I'm just looking at the screen right now.

TUTOR: Let's check your progress on the tracker.

STUDENT: I did some already. I'm just trying to get through the period.

TUTOR: The data shows you have only attempted two problems so far.

STUDENT: Yeah, I'm struggling the most with this, so I just guessed on two problems and stopped. I was hoping to just slide through the system today without doing the rest.

options.A: Describe an appropriate replacement behavior for the computer lab session, having the student practice this alternative positive skill immediately in a low-risk situation.
options.B: Use a gentle, non-directive approach with the student, emphasizing supportive comments rather than direct questions, and suggesting rather than instructing on the math skills.
options.C: Simplify the instructions for the assigned math skills and the five-in-a-row goal during the remainder of the computer lab session.
options.D: Project the real-time data on the screen so the student can compare their progress on the assigned math skills to their peers.
